newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - Weak demand to keep SE Asian prices soft.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Weak demand to keep SE Asian prices soft.

text.p: Southeast Asian rubber prices are expected to continue to trend lower this week, hammered by weak demand from major consumers like the United States, regional traders said on Monday.
"I do not see any improvement in demand next week as buyers, especially from the United States, seem to be well covered," an Indonesian dealer from Medan said.
"They are only likely to return to the market in a big way after the Christmas and New Year holidays," he added.

"Prices will be dead in the water if no fresh buying comes in. With many buyers normally going away during the Christmas holidays in December, it's going to be a very gloomy market," a Singapore-based trader said.
Dealers said agents from Singapore and Europe have been putting pressure on prices, bidding well below offers in an attempt to drive down prices.
"Sellers are trying to push prices below 55.00 (U.S.) cents in the key areas such as Medan, Palembang and Padang," one said.

Tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices eased 0.25-0.50 cents to end last week at 55.75-56.00 cents/lb FOB Medan, 55.25-55.50 cents FOB Surabaya, Padang and Palembang, 54.75-55.00 FOB Pontianak and Jambi. Latex remained unchanged at 2,300-2,400 rupiah/kg.
Slow demand and rising supply also continued to pressure Thai rubber market prices, trade sources said.
Rubber supplies entering the market rose by almost 40 percent last week although no figures were immediately available, trade and industry sources said.

"The prices are likely to move around this range or lower until the end of this year. The news on the surplus and high stocks will continue to dent demand," Sucharit Promdej, an advisor to the Rubber Research Center in Hat Yai, said.
"Buyers are not under pressure to buy due to anticipation that the surplus (in rubber stocks) will continue in 1997."

Heavy rainstorms hindering supplies from rubber plantations on the eastern coast of southern Thailand had no impact in the market because of increased rubber production in other areas, trade sources said.

The Thai benchmark RSS3 for January shipment was quoted at US$1.23-$1.24 a kg FOB Bangkok on Friday compared with around $1.25 earlier last week. STR 20 for January shipment was quoted unchanged at $1.23-$1.24 a kg on Friday, dealers said.
Latex prices eased slightly to 93 US cents a kg from about 95 cents last week.
In Malaysia, traders said they expect the benchmark RSS1 and SMR 20 rubber to trade in a tight range this week and probably lose one-half to one cent each in value due to poor consumer demand.
The December buying price for the benchmark RSS1 was at 319.50 Malaysian cents a kg at the close of the market last week while the SMR20 was at 308 cents.
"I expect the RSS1 and SMR20 to both lose about one-half to one cent this week as they're already quite low in value," a trader said.
Consumer demand was still weak in the Malaysian market and was not expected to improve much in the near term as buyers sat it out on expectations of further price falls.
Producers who were hoping for steady prices because of heavy rains hindering supplies of latex found it difficult to hold off on their sales, a trader said.
"It's a dilemma for the producers," said the trader, adding that supply of latex and other materials were still adequate for short-covering.
The Malaysian Meteorological Services Department said it expected the current week to be as rainy as the last.
Latex was quoted by trading houses at 238 Malaysian cents a kg on Friday.
(With contributions from Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia)
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
